item.title: Building a Conference Program
item.description: Plan a small conference, resolve scheduling conflicts, and communicate program changes to speakers and participants.

children.definition: A conference session intended for everyone at the event.
children.example: The opening plenary is the only session that needs seating for all 80 participants.

children.definition: A meeting in which a smaller group works or talks separately from the main conference group.
children.example: Limit the breakout session on staff training to 16 people so everyone has a chance to speak.
children.translation_ru: отдельная встреча или занятие в малой группе
children.translation_uz: kichik guruhda alohida oʻtkaziladigan muhokama yoki mashgʻulot

children.definition: A person who guides a discussion and decides when each speaker can contribute.
children.example: Ask the moderator to give both panelists a turn before inviting questions from the room.

children.definition: The period during which conference organizers accept proposals for talks or other sessions.
children.example: We extended the submission period by a week because several speakers needed more time to prepare their proposals.

children.definition: A written suggestion for a conference activity that explains its topic and how it will be organized.
children.example: The session proposal asks for movable seating because participants will work in groups of four.

children.definition: The group of people scheduled to speak at an event.
children.example: Please confirm the speaker lineup before we print the program with everyone’s name and job title.

children.definition: A period when two scheduled activities are happening at the same time.
children.example: There is a 15-minute overlap between the two sessions, and Lena is due to speak in both.

children.definition: A discussion in front of an audience in which a group of invited speakers share their views on a topic.
children.example: Move the panel discussion to the larger room so all four speakers can sit together at the front.
collocations: take part in a panel discussion

children.definition: The process of confirming that someone has arrived at an event.
children.example: To speed up check-in, we’ll use separate lists for speakers and other participants.

children.definition: The amount of time reserved for a particular activity.
children.example: The time allocation gives each of the three speakers 12 minutes and leaves six minutes for questions.

children.definition: A person invited to comment on a presentation and raise points for discussion.
children.example: Send the draft talks to the discussant on Monday so she can prepare her comments for Friday’s session.
children.translation_uz: maʼruzaga fikr bildirish uchun taklif etilgan mutaxassis

children.definition: A short summary at the end of an event, or the closing part in which that summary is given.
children.example: During the wrap-up, the organizer will summarize what each group agreed to do after the conference.

children.definition: A series of sessions on one theme that runs at the same time as another series.
children.example: The parallel track on staff training will run in Room B while the finance sessions continue in Room A.
children.translation_uz: boshqa turkum bilan bir vaqtda davom etadigan mavzuli sessiyalar turkumi

children.definition: An allotted time after a talk or panel when the audience can ask questions.
children.example: The question period starts as soon as the final speaker sits down.
children.translation_uz: tinglovchilar savol berishi uchun ajratilgan vaqt
